## Part 1

## IELTS Speaking Part 1 — to‘liq mashq banki

Birinchi 40 mavzu dastlabki ro‘yxatdagi tartibda berildi; undan keyin imtihon setlaridagi yangi Part 1 mavzulari keladi. Bir ma’noli savol variantlari birga berilgan. Javoblar O‘zbekistonda yashaydigan, ingliz tilini o‘rganayotgan o‘quvchi nuqtayi nazaridan yozilgan; shaxsiy faktlarni o‘zingizga moslang. Har javob taxminan 20–25 soniyalik mashq uchun; baholash balli kafolatlanmaydi.

### I qism. Asosiy 40 mavzu

### 1. Mirrors

#### 1. Do you like looking at yourself in a mirror?

**Javob:** Yes, briefly, before going out; it is more about checking that I look tidy than admiring myself. I usually **take a quick glance** to **check my appearance** before I leave home. It helps me **look presentable**, fits into my **daily routine**, and makes it easier to **make a good impression**.

## Part 2 — asosiy 59 mavzu

## IELTS Speaking Part 2 — 59 ta mavzu

Har mavzuga bitta to‘liq sample answer va uning ichida ishlatilgan aynan 10 ta collocation berilgan. Javoblar 250–305 so‘z oralig‘ida; taxminan daqiqasiga 115–130 so‘z tezlikda aytilsa, 2:15 atrofida davom etadi. Pauza va shaxsiy nutq tezligiga qarab muddat o‘zgaradi. Namuna personaning xotiralari va rejalari sizning hayotingizga moslab almashtirilishi kerak. Yuqori ball matnni yodlash bilan kafolatlanmaydi: grammatikani, so‘zlarni, talaffuzni va savolga javob berishni mashq qiling.

32-mavzudagi qonun nomi O‘zbekiston hukumatining rasmiy ro‘yxatida keltirilgan: https://gov.uz/en/eco/pages/laws . Qonun talqiniga oid aniq maslahat berilmaydi.

### 1. City — Describe a city you visited and would like to visit again

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 280 words)**

Last spring I spent a weekend in Samarkand with my family, and it is the city I would most like to revisit. I had seen photographs of its famous squares, but photographs had not prepared me for the atmosphere of the place. We arrived early, left our bags at a small guesthouse and went straight out to explore.

What struck me first was the contrast between its historic buildings and the ordinary life going on around them. At Registan Square, I found myself **taking in the architecture** rather than rushing to take pictures. Later, we **wandered through the streets**, stopped for tea and **tried the local food**. An elderly shopkeeper told us a little about the neighbourhood, and that **brief conversation** made the trip feel much more personal. By the time the sun went down, I had completely lost track of time.

If I returned, I would **set aside more time** for the smaller places I missed. On our first visit we had tried to **fit too much into one day**, so I would travel at a slower pace and perhaps visit a museum. What makes the city memorable is that it offers both a **sense of history** and a **lively atmosphere**. It also gave me the chance to **spend quality time** with my family. Even now, a photograph of that afternoon can **bring back vivid memories**.

On a second visit I would ask local people which ordinary places they enjoy, not just follow a list of landmarks. I might discover a neighbourhood café or a quiet street that I missed completely the first time. That would let me understand the city as more than a collection of beautiful buildings.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **taking in the architecture** — me’morchilikni sinchiklab tomosha qilmoq
2. **wandered through the streets** — ko‘chalar bo‘ylab bemalol sayr qildik
3. **tried the local food** — mahalliy taomlarni tatib ko‘rdik
4. **brief conversation** — qisqa suhbat
5. **set aside more time** — ko‘proq vaqt ajratmoq
6. **fit too much into one day** — bir kunga haddan tashqari ko‘p ishni sig‘dirmoq
7. **sense of history** — tarix nafasi
8. **lively atmosphere** — jonli muhit
9. **spend quality time** — mazmunli vaqt o‘tkazmoq
10. **bring back vivid memories** — yorqin xotiralarni qayta jonlantirmoq


---

### 2. Toy — Describe a toy you enjoyed playing with in your childhood

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 265 words)**

One childhood toy I remember especially well was a small box of building blocks. It wasn't an expensive set, but it gave me an extraordinary amount of entertainment. My parents had bought it for me when I was quite young, and I kept it for years, even after some pieces had gone missing.

I would spread the blocks across the floor and **build miniature houses** or bridges for my toy cars. The fun lay in the fact that there was no single correct result. If a tower collapsed, I could **start from scratch** and come up with a better design. Sometimes a friend would join me, and we would **make up stories** about the people living in our imaginary town. We usually **lost track of time** until someone called us for dinner.

Looking back, that simple toy did more than **keep me entertained**. It encouraged me to **use my imagination** and **solve small problems** without worrying about failure. Having built something with my own hands, I felt a genuine **sense of achievement**, even if the structure fell apart ten minutes later. I had other toys, of course, but the blocks **stood out in my memory** because I could change the game every day. They remind me that children often need the **freedom to experiment** more than they need a complicated toy.

I still think about that toy when I see a child being given something with dozens of instructions. The simplest pieces allowed us to invent our own rules. Had I received a completed model instead, I doubt I would remember it as clearly today.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **build miniature houses** — mitti uylar qurmoq
2. **start from scratch** — boshidan qayta boshlamoq
3. **make up stories** — hikoyalar o‘ylab topmoq
4. **lost track of time** — vaqt qanday o‘tganini sezmay qolardik
5. **keep me entertained** — meni ovutib turmoq
6. **use my imagination** — tasavvurimni ishga solmoq
7. **solve small problems** — kichik muammolarni hal qilmoq
8. **sense of achievement** — yutuq hissi
9. **stood out in my memory** — xotiramda alohida o‘rin oldi
10. **freedom to experiment** — tajriba qilib ko‘rish erkinligi

### 3. Film / Movie — Describe a film you enjoyed watching

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 292 words)**

The film I'd like to talk about is *The Martian*, which I watched at home one evening after a friend had recommended it. It's a fictional story about an astronaut who is accidentally left on Mars and has to survive until a rescue becomes possible. I expected an ordinary space adventure, but the film turned out to be much more engaging than that.

What held my attention was the way the main character **tackled one problem at a time**. Instead of giving up, he tried to **make the most of limited resources**, often with a surprisingly good sense of humour. The story also showed people on Earth **working towards a common goal**, even when they disagreed about the safest approach. Although I knew the plot was invented, the setbacks felt real enough to **keep me on the edge of my seat**. I was particularly impressed by the moments when a tiny calculation could have enormous consequences.

I enjoyed the film because it **struck a balance** between suspense, science and human warmth. It didn't pretend that determination alone could solve everything: the astronaut needed both his own skills and help from others. After the credits, I found myself **thinking about resilience** and how important it is to **stay calm under pressure**. I would happily watch it again, partly for the **visual effects**, but mainly for its message that **creative thinking** becomes most valuable when plans go wrong.

My favourite scene is the point at which the astronaut has to rethink a plan that seemed perfectly sound. It shows how **a fresh approach** can matter as much as technical knowledge. That combination of intelligence, uncertainty and humour gave the story a human quality I hadn't expected from a film set so far from Earth.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **tackled one problem at a time** — muammolarni birma-bir hal qildi
2. **make the most of limited resources** — cheklangan resurslardan unumli foydalanmoq
3. **working towards a common goal** — umumiy maqsad sari ishlayotgani
4. **keep me on the edge of my seat** — meni hayajonda ushlab turmoq
5. **struck a balance** — muvozanatni topdi
6. **thinking about resilience** — bardoshlilik haqida o‘ylash
7. **stay calm under pressure** — bosim ostida xotirjam qolmoq
8. **visual effects** — vizual effektlar
9. **creative thinking** — ijodiy fikrlash
10. **a fresh approach** — yangicha yondashuv

### 4. Place to recommend — Describe a place you would recommend living in, other than your hometown

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 275 words)**

I would recommend Samarkand as a place to live, at least for someone who enjoys history and doesn't mind a steady flow of visitors. I don't come from there, but I spent a few days in the city with my family. I realise a short visit cannot tell me everything about daily life, so this is a personal impression rather than a guarantee.

The first thing I noticed was how easy it was to **explore on foot** in the areas we visited. There were places to eat, small shops and spaces where people could **meet up with friends**. Its historic sites create a **distinctive character** that many newer places struggle to develop. At the same time, I saw families going about ordinary routines, which made it feel like a **lived-in city** rather than a museum. One evening, a local person gave us directions and then suggested a nearby place for tea; that **warm hospitality** stayed with me.

If I were thinking of moving there, I would first **look into the cost of living**, transport and study opportunities. Having said that, the city seems to offer a good **change of pace** for someone like me. I could imagine **settling into a routine** while still having interesting places to explore on weekends. For me, a good home is somewhere I can **feel at ease**, **build a community** and remain curious about my surroundings.

I would also tell someone considering a move to visit at an ordinary time, not only during a holiday. Seeing how people commute and buy groceries would provide a more honest picture. A recommendation is useful only when it includes practical questions alongside enthusiasm.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **explore on foot** — piyoda aylanib chiqmoq
2. **meet up with friends** — do‘stlari bilan uchrashmoq
3. **distinctive character** — o‘ziga xos qiyofa
4. **lived-in city** — odamlar kundalik yashaydigan shahar
5. **warm hospitality** — samimiy mehmondo‘stlik
6. **look into the cost of living** — yashash xarajatlarini o‘rganmoq
7. **change of pace** — hayot sur’atidagi yoqimli o‘zgarish
8. **settling into a routine** — kun tartibiga moslashib ketmoq
9. **feel at ease** — o‘zimni erkin his qilmoq
10. **build a community** — atrofimda yaqinlar davrasini yaratmoq

### 5. Quiet place — Describe a quiet place you like to be alone or would like to visit

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 284 words)**

There is a small park a short walk from my home where I like to spend time by myself. It isn't silent, but once I leave the main road, the traffic becomes a distant sound. There are a few benches under the trees, and I usually go there in the late afternoon when most people are on their way home.

On days when schoolwork starts to **pile up**, I take a book or just sit and **let my thoughts settle**. I sometimes **watch the light change** through the branches instead of looking at my phone. That sounds like a small thing, but it helps me **take a break from screens** and **clear my head**. Once, I had been struggling with an essay introduction for hours. After twenty minutes in the park, I returned home with a simpler idea that worked much better.

What I like most is that nobody expects me to do anything there. I can **enjoy my own company** without feeling lonely. If I had more time, I'd like to find a similar place in the countryside, with more trees and fewer cars. For now, though, this park is **within easy reach**, so I can visit it whenever I need to **slow down for a while**. It gives me a rare **sense of calm** in an otherwise busy week. That is why I keep going back rather than looking for a more impressive place.

Even when other people use the park, we tend to leave one another alone, which is part of its appeal. I do not need a perfectly empty space to feel peaceful. A place can still offer **a little privacy** if the people in it respect one another's quiet.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **pile up** — yig‘ilib ketmoq
2. **let my thoughts settle** — xayollarimni tinchlantirmoq
3. **watch the light change** — yorug‘lik o‘zgarishini kuzatmoq
4. **take a break from screens** — ekrandan tanaffus qilmoq
5. **clear my head** — xayolimni tiniqlashtirmoq
6. **enjoy my own company** — yolg‘iz qolishdan zavqlanmoq
7. **within easy reach** — oson yetib boriladigan joyda
8. **slow down for a while** — bir muddat sekinlashmoq
9. **sense of calm** — xotirjamlik hissi
10. **a little privacy** — biroz shaxsiylik

### 6. Local news — Describe a piece of local news that interested many people

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 274 words)**

One piece of local news that attracted attention where I live was an announcement about improving a busy neighbourhood road and the pedestrian crossing beside it. I heard about it first from relatives and then saw people discussing it in a local group. I can't recall every official detail, but the conversation around it was memorable.

That crossing is close to shops and a place where many students pass, so people had been **raising concerns** about traffic for some time. Some residents welcomed the proposed changes because they hoped it would **make the area safer**. Others were worried that construction might **disrupt daily travel** or affect nearby businesses. At home we talked about how even a modest road project can **have a direct impact** on families who use the route every day.

What made the story interesting to me was not the construction itself but the range of reactions. It reminded me that local news often **brings practical issues to light** that national headlines overlook. Ideally, officials would **listen to residents** and **keep people informed** as plans develop. I also learned to **check the original announcement** rather than rely on comments alone, because a rumour can spread quickly. Whether or not every suggestion is accepted, a public discussion gives people a chance to **voice their opinions** and perhaps improve the result.

I followed the story for a few days and noticed that the discussion became more specific once people had seen a proposed timetable. It reminded me to **distinguish facts from rumours** when a story affects my neighbourhood. What matters most is whether the eventual change actually helps the people who use that crossing.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **raising concerns** — xavotirlarini bildirish
2. **make the area safer** — hududni xavfsizroq qilish
3. **disrupt daily travel** — kundalik qatnovga xalaqit berish
4. **have a direct impact** — bevosita ta’sir ko‘rsatmoq
5. **brings practical issues to light** — amaliy muammolarni yuzaga chiqaradi
6. **listen to residents** — aholini tinglamoq
7. **keep people informed** — odamlarni xabardor qilib turmoq
8. **check the original announcement** — asl e’lonni tekshirmoq
9. **voice their opinions** — fikrlarini bildirmoq
10. **distinguish facts from rumours** — faktlarni mish-mishlardan ajratish

### 7. Story with animals — Describe an animal story or character

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 285 words)**

The animal story that has stayed with me is *The Lion and the Mouse*. I first heard it as a child and later came across it in English while practising reading. It is short enough to retell in a minute, yet it has a point that is easy to remember.

In the story, a lion catches a mouse but decides to **let it go**. The mouse promises to help one day, which sounds absurd because the lion is so much bigger. Later, when the lion gets trapped in a net, the mouse **comes to the rescue** and gnaws through the ropes. The moment **turns the tables**: the creature that seemed powerless becomes the only one able to help. As a child I enjoyed the surprise. As I grew older, I began to notice how neatly the story **challenges assumptions** about strength and usefulness.

The mouse is my favourite character because it **keeps its promise** without making a grand speech. The lion also deserves credit for showing mercy before there is anything to gain from it. If I were telling this story to a younger child, I would keep the language simple and ask what they would have done in the lion's place. The lesson I take from it is to **treat others with respect** and not **judge by appearances**. Although the plot is simple, its message can **stay with you** for years and **apply to everyday life**.

It is also a useful story for language learning because the characters and sequence are so clear. I can retell it in simple English, then try to express its meaning in a more nuanced way. That has helped me **practise storytelling** while thinking about the lesson behind it.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **let it go** — uni qo‘yib yubormoq
2. **comes to the rescue** — yordamga keladi
3. **turns the tables** — vaziyatni butunlay o‘zgartiradi
4. **challenges assumptions** — oldindan shakllangan fikrlarga qarshi chiqadi
5. **keeps its promise** — va’dasida turadi
6. **treat others with respect** — boshqalarga hurmat bilan munosabatda bo‘lmoq
7. **judge by appearances** — tashqi ko‘rinishga qarab baholamoq
8. **stay with you** — xotirada qolmoq
9. **apply to everyday life** — kundalik hayotga tatbiq etilmoq
10. **practise storytelling** — hikoya qilishni mashq qilish

### 8. Person who learns languages easily — Describe someone good at learning languages

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 278 words)**

I'd like to describe a classmate who seems to learn languages remarkably quickly. We became friends through English lessons, and I noticed that he could remember a new expression after hearing it only a couple of times. At first I assumed he simply had a natural gift, but seeing how he studies changed my mind.

He **picks up new words** from films and podcasts, then tries to **use them in conversation** on the same day. If he makes a mistake, he doesn't become embarrassed; he asks for a correction and **makes a mental note**. He also **switches between languages** without translating every sentence word for word. Once, while we were preparing a short presentation, he explained a difficult idea in two different ways until everyone understood it. What impressed me wasn't his accent but his ability to **get his point across**.

Watching him has taught me that apparent ease can hide a great deal of practice. He listens regularly, **reviews useful phrases** and looks for chances to speak outside class. I have tried to **follow his example** by recording myself and asking more questions. If I could learn one thing from him, it would be his willingness to **take risks with language**. He rarely lets the fear of an imperfect sentence **hold him back**, and that attitude seems to help him **make rapid progress**.

I used to compare my progress with his and feel discouraged. Then I realised that I was seeing the result of habits he had built over a long time. Now I ask him how he practises rather than simply telling him he is talented; his methods are more useful to me than a compliment.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **picks up new words** — yangi so‘zlarni tez o‘zlashtiradi
2. **use them in conversation** — ularni suhbatda ishlatmoq
3. **makes a mental note** — yodda tutib oladi
4. **switches between languages** — tillar o‘rtasida oson o‘tadi
5. **get his point across** — fikrini tushunarli yetkazmoq
6. **reviews useful phrases** — foydali iboralarni takrorlaydi
7. **follow his example** — undan o‘rnak olmoq
8. **take risks with language** — tilda xato qilishdan cho‘chimay sinab ko‘rmoq
9. **hold him back** — uni ortga tortmoq
10. **make rapid progress** — tez rivojlanmoq

### 9. Boring place — Describe a place you found boring

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 277 words)**

The place that comes to mind is a waiting area in an administrative building that I visited with a relative. I don't want to be unfair to the people working there; the building served a necessary purpose. From a visitor's point of view, however, it was an unusually dull place to spend an afternoon.

We had arrived early for an appointment, but the schedule was delayed and we ended up **waiting around** much longer than expected. The room had plain walls, rows of chairs and almost nothing to read. There was little **natural light**, and the slow movement of the queue made time seem to **drag on**. I tried to read on my phone, but the connection kept failing, so even that did not help. Eventually my relative and I **struck up a conversation** with another visitor, which at least made the experience feel less impersonal.

What made the place boring was less its appearance than the lack of information. Had we known how long the wait would be, we could have **made better use of our time**. A clear display, some seating near a window and regular updates would have **made a noticeable difference**. The experience taught me to **bring something to read** whenever I expect a queue. I also realised that a space can be **perfectly functional** yet still fail to **feel welcoming** or **hold your attention**.

I think about that visit whenever a place seems boring at first glance. Sometimes the surroundings are not the real problem; uncertainty and a lack of choice make the wait worse. Even a small notice telling visitors what to expect could have changed how we experienced that afternoon.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **waiting around** — bekor kutib o‘tirish

### 60. Family member to work with — Describe a family member you would like to work with in the future

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 281 words)**

I would like to work with my older cousin on a small educational project. She has helped organise family events, and I have seen how well she handles details without losing sight of what people need. I am interested in building a learning website, so I could imagine us working together for a short period rather than assuming that running a family business would automatically be easy.

I would focus on the technical side while she **kept the project organised** and **spoke to potential users**. Before creating anything substantial, we would **agree on clear roles** and ask a few students what they actually struggle with. If someone said the instructions were confusing, I hope we would **take the feedback seriously** instead of defending our first idea. My cousin is particularly good at **setting realistic deadlines**, which would help me avoid spending weeks polishing a feature nobody requested.

What appeals to me is the possibility of **combining our strengths**. At the same time, we would need to **keep work and family separate** when disagreements arose. I would want us to discuss a problem directly, not carry it into a family dinner. Even if the project never became a business, I think we could **learn from each other** and perhaps create something genuinely useful. The experience would teach me to **share responsibility** rather than try to do everything myself, and to **respect a different perspective**.

What I respect is his **willingness to change course**. Success did not come from a single brilliant idea; it came from noticing problems and responding to them. Watching him encouraged me to **deal with setbacks** without treating them as a verdict on my ability. ### 86. Shop you often visit — Describe a shop you go to regularly

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 264 words)**

A shop I visit fairly often is a small bookshop near a road I use on the way to class. It sells books, notebooks and a few everyday study supplies. I don't buy something on every visit; sometimes I just look at the new titles and make a note of what I might want to read later.

The owner has **arranged the shelves clearly**, so it is easy to **find a particular section**. I usually browse the English-learning books first, then look at the stationery. Once I asked for a book at a suitable level, and the owner **offered a helpful suggestion** without trying to sell me the most expensive option. I appreciated that she **took my budget into account**. I bought the book and returned after finishing it to see what else she would recommend.

I like the shop because it feels personal and easy to use. The staff **remember regular customers** but never make me feel obliged to spend money. If I am planning to buy something, I still **compare prices** and think about whether I need it. But I enjoy **supporting a local business** when the service is good. The place has become part of my weekly routine: a short visit helps me **discover new books** and **stay curious about reading**, even during busy study periods.

The owner sometimes displays short notes beside new books, and those notes have introduced me to subjects I would not have searched for online. They are small details, but they **make browsing enjoyable**. I often leave with a new idea even if I buy nothing.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **arranged the shelves clearly** — javonlarni tushunarli tartiblagan
2. **find a particular section** — kerakli bo‘limni topish
3. **offered a helpful suggestion** — foydali tavsiya berdi
4. **took my budget into account** — budjetimni hisobga oldi
5. **remember regular customers** — doimiy mijozlarni eslab qoladi
6. **compare prices** — narxlarni solishtiraman
7. **supporting a local business** — mahalliy biznesni qo‘llab-quvvatlash
8. **discover new books** — yangi kitoblarni kashf qilish
9. **stay curious about reading** — o‘qishga qiziqishni saqlash
10. **make browsing enjoyable** — kitoblarni ko‘zdan kechirishni yoqimli qiladi

---

### 87. Changed your opinion — Describe a time you changed your mind about something

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 273 words)**

I changed my opinion about studying with other people. For a long time I assumed group study was mostly a chance to talk and lose focus. I preferred working alone and avoided invitations to revise with classmates. Then I joined a small group before an English exam because I was struggling with one part of the reading section.

We **agreed on a clear goal**: each of us would try a short passage independently, then explain the questions we had answered differently. That structure prevented the meeting from becoming casual conversation. When I explained my choice, a classmate **pointed out a clue** I had missed in the text. In return, I helped another student understand why a similar-looking phrase did not support her answer. We **learned from each other's mistakes** and finished the session with a clearer idea of what to practise next.

I did not suddenly decide that every group is effective. Without a goal, a study session can still **drift off topic**. But that experience made me **reconsider my assumption**. I now study alone when I need quiet concentration and **work with others** when discussion can reveal something I have overlooked. Changing my mind felt slightly uncomfortable because I had been so certain. In the end, I was glad I had **given it a fair try**. It taught me to **stay open to evidence** and **avoid judging too quickly**.

I have since used the same approach with another assumption: I first ask what evidence might change my view. That does not mean I abandon my opinion whenever someone disagrees. It means I can **test an idea fairly** rather than protect it automatically.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **agreed on a clear goal** — aniq maqsadga kelishib oldik
2. **pointed out a clue** — muhim ishorani ko‘rsatdi
3. **learned from each other's mistakes** — bir-birimizning xatolarimizdan o‘rgandik
4. **drift off topic** — mavzudan chetga chiqish
5. **reconsider my assumption** — avvalgi fikrimni qayta ko‘rib chiqish
6. **work with others** — boshqalar bilan ishlash
7. **given it a fair try** — uni xolis sinab ko‘rganim
8. **stay open to evidence** — dalillarga ochiq bo‘lish
9. **avoid judging too quickly** — shoshilib baho bermaslik
10. **test an idea fairly** — fikrni xolis sinab ko‘rish

---

### 88. Woke up early — Describe an occasion when you got up very early

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 287 words)**

One morning I got up much earlier than usual to travel with my family to Samarkand. We wanted to arrive with enough time to enjoy the day without rushing from place to place. My alarm went off while it was still dark, and for a moment I wondered why I had agreed to the plan.

I **got ready in silence** so I would not wake anyone who was still sleeping. We **set off before sunrise** with a simple breakfast packed for the journey. At first I was sleepy, but watching the sky become brighter through the window gradually **lifted my mood**. There were fewer vehicles on the road, and we could **travel at a steady pace**. By the time we arrived, the city was becoming busy and we had almost the whole day ahead of us.

Getting up early was worth it because it gave us **more time to explore**. We could stop for tea and **take our time** rather than constantly check a schedule. I did feel tired later in the afternoon, so I would not make a habit of sleeping too little. Had we left several hours later, we might have spent more of the trip worrying about what to miss. The experience showed me that an early start can **make a day feel longer** when it is planned sensibly. I went to bed early that evening with **vivid memories** of the journey.

I remember stopping for a quick breakfast after arriving and feeling pleased that we were not already behind schedule. The early start had **taken some pressure off**. If I repeated the trip, I would still prepare the night before so the morning remained calm. I would also **make time to rest** later.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **got ready in silence** — shovqin qilmasdan tayyorlandim
2. **set off before sunrise** — quyosh chiqmasidan yo‘lga tushdik
3. **lifted my mood** — kayfiyatimni ko‘tardi
4. **travel at a steady pace** — bir maromda harakatlanish
5. **more time to explore** — aylanish uchun ko‘proq vaqt
6. **take our time** — shoshilmaslik
7. **make a day feel longer** — kunni uzunroq his qildirish
8. **vivid memories** — yorqin xotiralar
9. **taken some pressure off** — bir oz bosimni kamaytirdi
10. **make time to rest** — dam olishga vaqt ajratish

### 89. Successful sportsperson — Describe an athlete who performed well in an important event

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 277 words)**

A sportsperson whose performance impressed me is a young player I watched in a local football final. I do not know his name well enough to give a full biography, and the match was not a national event. What stayed with me was how he behaved when his team was under pressure.

In the first half he missed a good chance, and the crowd reacted loudly. For a moment he looked disappointed, but he **got back into the game** and continued to **support his teammates**. Later, when the other team pressed forward, he made a careful pass that **created an opening**. A teammate scored from the move. I was impressed that he did not **try to take all the credit** afterwards; he pointed to the team and the work they had done in training. The final minutes were tense, but they **held on to their lead**.

I call his performance successful because it involved more than one good moment. He **recovered from a mistake**, **made a smart decision under pressure** and helped others play well. I cannot know how he felt inside, but from the stands he appeared determined rather than panicked. The event reminded me that an important performance is rarely perfect. What counts is whether you can **stay involved** when something goes wrong and **contribute to a shared result**. I left the match admiring his attitude as much as his skill.

A younger player nearby watched him after the missed chance and applauded when he made the decisive pass. That response stayed with me. The athlete had **set an example** by continuing to contribute when it would have been easy to dwell on one error.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **got back into the game** — yana o‘yinga qaytdi
2. **support his teammates** — jamoadoshlarini qo‘llab-quvvatlash
3. **created an opening** — hujum uchun imkon yaratdi
4. **try to take all the credit** — barcha maqtovni o‘ziga olish
5. **held on to their lead** — ustunlikni saqlab qolishdi
6. **recovered from a mistake** — xatodan keyin o‘zini tikladi
7. **made a smart decision under pressure** — bosim ostida oqilona qaror qildi
8. **stay involved** — faol qatnashib qolish
9. **contribute to a shared result** — umumiy natijaga hissa qo‘shish
10. **set an example** — namuna ko‘rsatdi

### 90. Article about a health problem — Describe a health-related article you read

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 264 words)**

I read an article about how poor sleep can affect concentration in teenagers. I found it while looking for ways to organise my study routine, since I had noticed that staying up late made difficult reading passages feel even harder the next day. The article was written for a general audience, not as personal medical advice, and I read it with that distinction in mind.

It discussed the link between sleep and attention and suggested **keeping a regular schedule**. I liked that it **explained the reasoning** rather than offering a dramatic shortcut. At the same time, I **checked the source** because online health claims can sound confident even when they are weakly supported. I also noticed that the piece did not pretend every tired student has the same problem. If someone has persistent symptoms, a general article cannot **replace professional advice**.

What I took from the article was a practical question: was I **giving myself enough time to sleep** before blaming my concentration on a difficult subject? For a week I tried to **put my phone away earlier** and **notice the difference**. That small experiment did not answer every question about health, but it helped me **pay attention to my habits**. I would recommend reading such articles critically, **avoiding sweeping claims** and **asking for help when needed**.

I would be careful not to draw a medical conclusion from my own one-week experiment. The article helped me ask better questions about my routine; it did not diagnose a condition. For any ongoing difficulty, I would seek qualified guidance rather than rely on a single webpage.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **keeping a regular schedule** — muntazam uyqu tartibini saqlash
2. **explained the reasoning** — sababini tushuntirdi
3. **checked the source** — manbani tekshirdim
4. **replace professional advice** — mutaxassis maslahatining o‘rnini bosish
5. **giving myself enough time to sleep** — o‘zimga yetarli uxlash vaqtini ajratayotgan edimmi
6. **put my phone away earlier** — telefonimni ertaroq chetga qo‘yish
7. **notice the difference** — farqni kuzatish
8. **pay attention to my habits** — odatlarimga e’tibor berish
9. **avoiding sweeping claims** — haddan tashqari umumiy da’volardan saqlanish
10. **asking for help when needed** — zarur bo‘lsa yordam so‘rash

### 91. Worked with others on a project — Describe a time you collaborated on a project

**Sample answer (~2:15 at a measured pace; 276 words)**

I once worked with two classmates on a short presentation about reducing waste at school. We were given a week and had to explain one practical change rather than list every environmental problem. At first we had different ideas: one person wanted posters, another wanted more bins, and I wanted to focus on how students could find clear information.

We **divided the work fairly** after agreeing on a shared aim. I drafted the outline, one classmate gathered examples and the other prepared the slides. Halfway through, we realised that our presentation had become too broad. We **cut less relevant points** and **built a clearer argument** around labelled collection points and simple instructions. We then **rehearsed together** so the transitions between speakers would feel natural. When one slide failed to load, we **made a backup version** rather than hope the problem would disappear.

On the day, each person knew what to say, and the teacher asked a useful question about who would maintain the collection points. We had not fully considered that, so we **admitted the limitation** and suggested discussing it with school staff. That answer was more honest than pretending our plan was complete. The project taught me to **listen to different ideas** and **solve problems as a team**. I enjoyed seeing how separate pieces of work could **come together** when we **kept a common goal in mind**.

After the presentation, we kept the slides and notes in a shared folder so each of us could review the feedback. Our idea needed more thought, but the process had strengthened our teamwork. I would happily work with them again on a project with a clearer, manageable scope.

**10 collocations va tarjimasi**

1. **divided the work fairly** — ishni adolatli taqsimladik
2. **cut less relevant points** — kamroq aloqador fikrlarni olib tashladik
3. **built a clearer argument** — aniqroq dalil tuzdik
4. **rehearsed together** — birga mashq qildik
5. **made a backup version** — zaxira versiya tayyorladik
6. **admitted the limitation** — cheklovni tan oldik
7. **listen to different ideas** — turli g‘oyalarni tinglash
8. **solve problems as a team** — muammolarni jamoa bo‘lib hal qilish
9. **come together** — bir butunga aylanish
10. **kept a common goal in mind** — umumiy maqsadni yodda tutdik

## Part 3 — asosiy 45 mavzu

## IELTS Speaking Part 3 — 45 mavzu, barcha 481 savol

Savollar yuborilgan fayldagi tartibda. Har biri 35–40 soniyalik mashq uchun taxminan 75–90 so‘zdan iborat. Turli tezlik va pauzalar davomiylikni o‘zgartiradi. Javoblarda savolga bevosita fikr, sabab, misol va cheklov berilgan; mavzu bo‘yicha bir necha savol bir xil foydali iboralarni takrorlaydi. Har bir javobdagi 3 ta qalin ibora tagida o‘zbekchaga tarjima qilingan. Bu sample answerlar yodlash yoki muayyan IELTS bandini kafolatlash uchun emas; fikrni o‘zingizning ovozingiz bilan tushuntirishni mashq qiling.

Sog‘liq va ekran odatlari haqidagi umumiy jumlalar uchun CDC: https://www.cdc.gov/healthy-schools/digital-behaviors/index.html . Iqlim va suv resurslari haqidagi umumiy jumlalar uchun IPCC: https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/chapter/chapter-10/ .

### 1. Cities / Visiting cities

#### 1. What makes a city attractive to visitors?

**Answer:** Attractive cities usually offer interesting places alongside practical ways to reach and enjoy them. A city is shaped by **public transport**, **access to services** and the quality of its **shared spaces**. Those features affect residents as much as visitors. For instance, a reliable bus route can make a distant school or market feel close. Still, the best solution depends on a city's size, budget and existing neighbourhoods. For example, a shaded square gives families somewhere to meet without spending money.

**Iboralar:** **public transport** — jamoat transporti; **access to services** — xizmatlardan foydalanish imkoniyati; **shared spaces** — umumiy jamoat joylari.

#### 2. Why do some people prefer visiting cities instead of the countryside?

### 2. Toys

#### 1. Are toys for boys and girls different?

**Answer:** I would avoid labelling toys strictly by gender, since children can enjoy the same creative activities. Good toys encourage **creative play**, **problem-solving skills** and **social interaction**. A child often learns most when there is room to invent different ways to play. Building blocks, for example, can become a bridge one day and a house the next. Of course, a toy's value also depends on how it is used and the child's age. A simple board game can teach children to take turns and adapt when they lose.

**Iboralar:** **creative play** — ijodiy o‘yin; **problem-solving skills** — muammoni hal qilish ko‘nikmalari; **social interaction** — ijtimoiy muloqot.

### 3. Films / Movies

#### 1. Why do some films become more popular than others?

**Answer:** Some films spread because their story is easy to discuss and viewers recommend them to friends. A film succeeds when **compelling storytelling**, **convincing performances** and an appropriate **viewing experience** come together. Audience preferences and budgets still vary. A quiet character scene can stay with viewers longer than an expensive action sequence. However, popularity does not automatically mean a film is artistically strong. For instance, a strong script may make viewers care even when the cast is unfamiliar.

### 5. Local news & Personal identity

#### 1. Do you think local news is important?

**Answer:** Yes, it helps residents understand changes that affect the places they actually use. Local reporting helps people **stay informed**, **make practical decisions** and **hold institutions accountable**. A useful story should explain how a change affects daily life. A report on a road closure, for instance, can help families plan their journeys. But people should check the source before sharing a dramatic local claim. News about a new clinic can tell residents where to seek a local service.

#### 4. What is personal identity?

**Answer:** It is a person's sense of who they are, shaped by relationships, experiences and values. Personal identity grows through **family history**, **shared traditions** and **individual choices**. Learning about it can help a person understand where they come from without limiting who they become. Choosing a local craft can connect someone with a place and its makers. Buying an imported product does not erase someone's cultural background. A grandparent's story can make a familiar custom more meaningful to a child.

**Iboralar:** **family history** — oila tarixi; **shared traditions** — umumiy an’analar; **individual choices** — shaxsiy tanlovlar.

Animal stories can nurture **empathy for living things**, encourage **curiosity about nature** and offer **memorable life lessons**. The characters make complex ideas easier to discuss. A story about a pet can start a conversation about daily care and responsibility.

### 8. Boring places / Boredom

#### 1. Is being bored always a bad thing?

**Answer:** Not always; a quiet gap can lead to reflection or a new idea. Boredom can signal a lack of **mental stimulation**, **personal choice** or **a clear purpose**. It can be uncomfortable, yet it sometimes prompts a person to try something new. An empty waiting area feels longer when visitors have no idea when they will be seen. That does not mean every quiet moment needs to be filled with entertainment. A waiting room feels worse when nobody knows how long the delay will be.

**Iboralar:** **mental stimulation** — aqliy rag‘bat; **personal choice** — shaxsiy tanlov; **a clear purpose** — aniq maqsad.

### 9. Business / Successful business people

#### 1. What qualities make a person successful in business?

**Answer:** Successful owners listen to customers, manage money carefully and keep learning from mistakes. A viable business needs to **understand customer needs**, **manage financial risks** and **adapt to changing conditions**. A clever idea matters less if nobody can use it. A small shop might keep customers by offering dependable service and clear prices. Of course, funding and local conditions also affect what is possible. An online service can improve when its owner listens to recurring complaints.

### 10. Advertisements

#### 1. Should advertisements be different for different age groups?

**Answer:** Yes, the language and examples should suit the audience without exploiting younger viewers. Advertising can **raise awareness**, **shape expectations** and **influence purchasing decisions**. Its usefulness depends on whether the claims are clear and the product meets real needs. A practical demonstration gives buyers more to judge than a celebrity endorsement. Even persuasive marketing cannot compensate for poor quality over time. A brief advertisement can introduce a service that local customers had not known about. The immediate result matters, but we should also consider how the effects develop over time.

### 11. Growing plants / Gardening

#### 1. Are bikes popular in your city?

**Answer:** Bicycles appeal to some people for short trips, but safe routes and distance matter. A transport system should balance **affordability**, **road safety** and **environmental impact**. What works in a compact centre may not work in a remote village. A safe cycle lane can make a short urban journey possible without a car. Yet improvements need to reflect distance, weather and local demand. A reliable rural bus can connect people with work, school and healthcare. The immediate result matters, but we should also consider how the effects develop over time.

An opinion is most useful when it helps someone think, not just please the speaker. A teacher might praise a strong example before suggesting a clearer conclusion. However, timing and tone matter as much as the message. A friend could explain which part of a presentation was hard to follow.

### 17. Technology

#### 1. What kinds of technology do people want to own nowadays?

**Answer:** People often want devices that help them work, learn or communicate more conveniently. Technology can **save time**, **improve access to information** and **support everyday tasks**. The benefit depends on how reliably a tool works and who can use it. A laptop can help a student research and revise a document efficiently. Still, practical training matters for people unfamiliar with the device. A navigation app can make an unfamiliar journey less stressful. The immediate result matters, but we should also consider how the effects develop over time.

**Iboralar:** **save time** — vaqtni tejash; **improve access to information** — ma’lumotga kirishni yaxshilash; **support everyday tasks** — kundalik ishlarni yengillashtirish.

### 22. Memory / Learning

#### 1. Is it important to memorize things nowadays?

**Answer:** Basic facts matter, but memorising without understanding has limited value. Memory works best when people **understand the idea**, **revisit information** and **connect it to real use**. Devices can store facts, but they do not replace judgement. A student who explains a concept aloud often recalls it better than one who rereads it. The right balance changes with the subject and the person's needs. A calendar is useful for dates, while understanding helps with unfamiliar problems.

## Part 3 — qo‘shimcha 84 to‘plam

## IELTS Speaking Part 3 — yangi fayldagi 84 to‘plam, 548 savol

Fayl imtihon yozuvlaridagi barcha Part 3 savollarini asl tartibida qamrab oladi. Ayrim savollar aynan takrorlangan: javoblar to‘plamlar tartibini saqlash uchun qayta keltirilgan. Har bir inglizcha namunaviy javob taxminan 75–90 so‘z bo‘lib, 35–40 soniyalik mashq uchun mo‘ljallangan; haqiqiy vaqt nutq tezligiga bog‘liq. Har bir javob ostida uchta ishlatilgan ibora va ularning o‘zbekcha tarjimasi bor. Bir mavzudagi javoblarda mashqni yengillashtirish uchun ayrim iboralar va misollar takrorlanadi. Javoblar band 9 bahosiga kafolat emas; fikr, mantiq, ravonlik va talaffuzni o‘z nutqingizda mashq qiling.

Sog‘liq haqidagi umumiy mavzular uchun qo‘shimcha ma’lumot: [WHO — healthy diet](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/healthy-diet), [WHO — physical activity](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/physical-activity), [CDC — about sleep](https://www.cdc.gov/sleep/about/).

#### 1. Do you think it is a good idea for family members to work together?

**Sample answer:** Yes, shared trust can make family collaboration effective, provided everyone has a clear role. A family firm can build **mutual trust**, rely on **shared responsibility** and pass down **practical experience**. However, personal bonds need clear professional boundaries. For instance, relatives may divide accounting and customer service according to their strengths. Yet an argument at work should not become a dispute at the dinner table. A parent can teach a child the trade before the child decides whether to join.
